Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/notebooks/ipywidgets
Fetched: 2026-06-17

Overview:
"ipywidgets are visual elements that allow users to specify parameter values in notebook cells."
"over 30 different controls, including form controls such as sliders, text boxes, and checkboxes, as well as layout controls such as tabs, accordions, and grids."

== Version support ==

Preview: "ipywidgets are available in preview in Databricks Runtime 11.0 through Databricks Runtime 12.2 LTS"
GA: "generally available in Databricks Runtime 13.0 and above"
Unity Catalog: "Support for Unity Catalog tables is available in Databricks Runtime 12.1 and above on Unity Catalog-enabled clusters"

Known issue: "Some ipywidgets do not work in Databricks Runtime 15.0"

== Browser requirement ==

"your browser must be able to access the databricks-dev-cloudfront.dev.databricks.com domain"

== Port configuration ==

Default port: 6062
"With Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS and above, if you run into conflicts with third-party integrations such as Datadog, you can change the port"
Spark config: spark.databricks.driver.ipykernel.commChannelPort <port-number>
"The Spark config must be set when the cluster is created."

== ipywidgets vs Databricks widgets ==

"You can use Databricks widgets to pass parameters between notebooks and to pass parameters to jobs; ipywidgets do not support these scenarios"
Databricks recommends ipywidgets for Python; use Databricks widgets for other languages.

== Third-party widgets ==

"Databricks provides best-effort support for third-party widgets" — ipyleaflet, bqplot, VegaFusion
"some third-party widgets aren't supported"

== Code examples ==

1. Histogram with interact slider:
```python
import ipywidgets as widgets
from ipywidgets import interact
sparkDF = spark.read.csv("/databricks-datasets/bikeSharing/data-001/day.csv", header="true", inferSchema="true")
# (bins=(3, 10) defines an integer slider widget that allows values between 3 and 10.
@interact(bins=(3, 10))
def plot_histogram(bins):
  pdf = sparkDF.toPandas()
  pdf.hist(column='temp', bins=bins)
```

2. IntSlider:
```python
import ipywidgets as widgets
int_slider = widgets.IntSlider(max=10, value=5)
int_slider
```

3. Button with Unity Catalog (DBR 12.1+):
```python
import ipywidgets as widgets
button = widgets.Button(description="Load dataframe sample")
output = widgets.Output()
def load_sample_df(table_name):
  return spark.sql(f"SELECT * FROM {table_name} LIMIT 1000")
def on_button_clicked(_):
    with output:
      output.clear_output()
      df = load_sample_df('<catalog>.<schema>.<table>')
      print(df.toPandas())
button.on_click(on_button_clicked)
display(button, output)
```
